title: Sub-formula identity codes: every ')' carries a 31-bit +-1 code of the bracket span it closes (polynomial rolling hash of the span's tokens), added to the input embedding through a learned Linear(31, 384), on the 191-claude incumbent (9,569,664 params)
description: Idea ID: none in the P01-P50 backlog; a new mechanism in the family of 150-fable's Engram-lite input table (Robbie's DeepSeek lead: hashed n-gram features) and of the structural-position runs 170/179, extended from fixed n-grams to whole bracket spans. The model computes, inside its forward and from the token ids alone (tokenizer, data, RL and eval untouched), a rolling hash of the tokens between every ')' and its matching '(' and adds a learned linear map of the hash's 31 bits (as +-1) to that ')' token's embedding, so two occurrences of the same sub-formula anywhere in the context carry the same feature. Natural-deduction steps are formula-equality tests (modus ponens needs a line equal to an implication's antecedent, and-intro writes two earlier formulas side by side), which a 6-block transformer must otherwise rebuild token by token through attention, and that gets harder as proofs grow past the pretraining cap of 6 lines (more lines, more near-identical n-grams of brackets and four atoms); with identity codes a content (NoPE) head can match equal sub-formulas in one hop at any distance, which should raise the share of valid long proofs that expert iteration samples and learns from. Open registrations checked: none besides this one (192-claude and 193-fable are recorded).
hypothesis: Mechanism: formula identity is the bottleneck feature for proofs longer than the pretraining cap. Every proof line restates formulas that are copies or compositions of earlier sub-formulas, and rule applicability is an equality test between spans of up to ~40 tokens drawn from an alphabet of 11 formula tokens, so local n-grams are highly ambiguous and the ambiguity grows with the number of lines in context. A per-span code that is identical for identical spans and near-orthogonal otherwise (31 random-looking bits: matching codes give a dot product of 31, different ones ~0 +- 5.6) turns the test into one attention hop. The code depends on span content only (prefix-sum hash times the inverse power of the span's start), so it is invariant to position, line number and proof length, and nothing about it is tied to proofs of <= 6 lines. It is random per distinct sub-formula, so the 31-dim projection can only support equality matching, not memorised per-formula semantics. Evidence before the run (two 60 s bench probes, not evidence for a keep): the candidate reached val loss 0.0816 after 417 steps and 0.0903 after 478 steps with sample accuracy 0.021 and 0.063, where 188-fable's bench of the incumbent architecture had val 0.109 after 290 steps with sample accuracy 0.002 and 193-fable's bench of the no-MTP model val 0.0846 after ~850 steps. So the codes appear to speed up early learning, by an amount two noisy probes do not pin down; whether that survives four rounds of expert iteration is the question, since 190/191/193 showed round-1 strength is recoverable and not a proxy for the metric. Risks: (1) spans that are not formulas (binders `( h1 : A )`, `( fun ... )` terms, whose hashes include shifted name tokens) get codes too, which are unique noise at those ')' positions; (2) sampling gets slower by the bracket tracking (done on the CPU during cached decoding: second bench 169 samples/s against 191's bench 194 and 193's 168) and a slow pod could push a seed towards the 2,400 s cap; (3) the other input-feature runs at width 384 (155 low-rank bigram 668, 157 factored trigram 667) lost ~20 to the incumbent, so table-like shortcuts may hurt what RL learns; this feature has 11,904 parameters instead of ~400k and encodes identity, not statistics. Decision rule fixed now: keep only if the 3-seed mean is strictly above 191's 683.67 (the change adds 63 lines, so a tie or ~0 is a discard under the simplicity rule); if the other agent keeps a file first, record.py's rule applies.
expected_delta: -20 to +45 vs 191's 683.7 (central +10). Pretraining 5,100-5,450 steps in 300 s per seed (benches: first step at 33-37 s, then 20.1-20.3 steps/s, i.e. the incumbent's per-step cost; 191: 5,362/5,298/5,220), ~4.5-4.8 epochs; val loss at the 75 s curve point below 191 seed 0's 0.0975 on 2+ seeds and final val loss 0.065-0.088 (191: 0.082-0.092); held-out greedy after pretraining 0.965-0.995 (191: 0.959-0.972); round-1 RL targets solved 500-900 (191: 682/454/225) and round-4 RL-solved 1,150-1,260 (191 mean 1,164); handoff n_params 9,569,664 exactly; RL sampling 130-215 samples/s (191: 152-228; bench 169 vs 194) and totals 1,800-2,200 s of 2,400. Falsifiers: final val loss above 0.088 on 2+ seeds (the codes do not help even pretraining); a 3-seed mean below 665 (the feature hurts what expert iteration reaches, as the 155/157 tables did); any seed over 2,300 s (the bracket tracking costs more than measured). Where a gain should show if the mechanism is right: eval bins 10-12 (191 seed 0: 84/219, 22/49, 4/54), where proofs are longest, rather than bins 7-9.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, the 191-claude model plus sub-formula identity codes added to the token embedding at the input
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 191-claude: ALiBiGPT gains code_proj = Linear(31, 384, bias=False) (init normal std 0.02) and the method span_codes(idx, cache); features() computes x = emb(idx) + code_proj(span_codes(idx)) before block 0, in every forward (pretraining, MTP trunk pass, RL fine-tune, sampling). span_codes: opens/closes are token ids 2 '(' and 3 ')' (asserted against tok.stoi in pretrain()); depth = cumsum(opens - closes); the bracket level of a token is depth (+1 for a ')'), clamped to [0, 31]; the matching '(' of a ')' is the latest '(' of the same level (cummax of its index over a (B, T, 32) one-hot); the span hash is sum_k (token_k + 1) * R^(k - i) mod P over the span [i, j], computed as (prefix_j - prefix_{i-1}) * R^(-i) mod P from int64 prefix sums, with P = 2^31 - 1, R = 1,000,003 and 4,096 precomputed powers and inverse powers (non-persistent buffers, rebuilt deterministically at construction); the feature is the hash's 31 bits as +-1 / sqrt(31) at ')' tokens with a matching '(' and the zero vector at every other token, so at init it has the token embedding's element scale (std 0.02). The MTP module's next-token embedding input still uses model.emb alone. Blocks, heads, ALiBi slopes, MTP, optimizers, schedule, batches, compile recipe and handoff unchanged. 63 insertions, 1 deletion (pretrain.py 428 -> 490 lines)
arch.n_params_detail: 191-claude's 9,557,760 + code_proj.weight 31 x 384 = 11,904 -> 9,569,664 (CPU check with fork 51604b3 and the A40 bench both report 9,569,664), under the 10M cap. MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff): 1,875,584 as in 191
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: 191-claude's module tree plus one state_dict key `code_proj.weight` (384, 31); the hash power tables and the slopes buffer are non-persistent and rebuilt by the constructor; score_holdout.py's zero-budget pretrain() call builds the same module tree
arch.kv_cache: unchanged per-block k/v and caches[0]['pos']; new CPU-side state in caches[0]: span_n (tokens seen), span_hash (B,) prefix hash, span_depth (B,), span_open_i / span_open_h (B, 32) index and prefix hash of the latest '(' of every level. With caches the ids go to the CPU, span_codes runs there with the same code as the full forward, and the (B, T, 31) codes come back to the device. CPU checks on 64 training records: vectorised hash equals a naive stack-based Python hash at every ')' (0 mismatching rows); left-padded prefill + one token at a time vs the full forward: max abs logit difference 1.5e-6 over 41 steps on 16 rows; one cached step's span_codes at 1,024 rows takes 0.30 ms on a laptop CPU, the 1,024 x 150 prefill 42 ms; on the A40 pod the CPU path sampled 169 samples/s against 120 with the bracket tracking on the GPU

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock from step 1, no warmup (unchanged from 191): lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same cosine fraction as AdamW from step 1, no warmup (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, the new code_proj.weight (31 -> 384 input feature map, same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as the embedding), all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights plus code_proj.weight; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining, unchanged; code_proj.weight is not a Muon matrix (it is not in model.blocks); the handoff model's parameters are 9,569,664

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged (the 200-step warmup those runs had is removed in 191, see optimizer.schedule). The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.compile: per-block torch.compile(dynamic=True), coalesce_tiling_analysis off, undone at handoff; Muon step as one CUDA graph; fused AdamW; batch max length from host
config.init: unchanged rule from 191: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)); LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0; new code_proj.weight normal std 0.02 (its draw comes after the fork GPT's own init, so emb/head draws equal 191's per seed; the blocks' draws shift)

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40, twice (probes, not evidence). First bench, bracket tracking on the GPU in every path: 417 steps in 60.3 s, first step at 37 s, 304 steps from 45 to 60 s = 20.3 steps/s (191's bench: ~20.8), peak 7.48 GB, n_params 9,569,664, train 0.147 / val 0.0816 at 60 s, sample_acc 0.0212, dynamo 3 unique graphs, but sampling 120 samples/s against 191's bench 194: the ~60 tiny CUDA ops per decoded token cost ~3 ms per step. Second bench, this exact file (cached decoding runs span_codes on the CPU; training and RL fine-tuning keep the GPU path): 478 steps in 60.2 s, first step at 33 s, 302 steps from 45 to 60 s = 20.1 steps/s, peak 7.43 GB, n_params 9,569,664, train 0.106 / val 0.0903 at 60 s, sample_acc 0.0625, sampling 169 samples/s (191's bench 194, 193's 168, 188's 201), dynamo 3 unique graphs, no recompiles counted, torch 2.9.1+cu129. Both pods booted only after A40 capacity retries (466 s and ~8 min). make -C code check clean
config.init_rng: data order and shift-augmentation draws equal 191's per seed (same generators); emb/head initial draws equal 191's; code_proj's normal draw precedes the blocks' init, so block and MTP initial matrices differ from 191's: seed pairs are ordinary pairs
